newsitem.title: USA: Dlr/mark ends higher in US following strong data.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark ends higher in US following strong data.

text.p: The dollar surged to a near eight-year high versus the German mark on Friday, as fresh evidence of strength in the U.S. job markets and manufacturing sector revived expectations of higher interest rates ahead.
Such concern hurt Treasuries as well and the 30-year bond lost more than two points, with its yield soaring to 6.46 percent from 6.30 percent on Thursday.
The Dow Jones industrial average suffered up to triple-digit losses to end down 28.57 points at 8194.04.
Mark/yen was heavily traded and retreated sharply as the yen benefitted from the mark's weakness.
This curbed the advance of dollar/yen which peaked at 119.10, its highest level since May 14, past a key technical resistance at 119.00.
Traders said fears that Japanese officials would resort to verbal intervention -- at least -- to defend their currency prevented the dollar from scoring sharp gains versus the yen.

"I think there is greater fear of the Bank of Japan than of the Bundesbank. This has forced a lot of demand for the yen against the Deutschemark," said Mike Malpede, senior analyst at Refco Group Ltd.

John Hazelton, chief dealer at Manufacturers and Traders Bank, said the dollar has not scored impressive gains versus the yen due to market fears that U.S. and Japanese officials favor an exchange rate no higher than 120 yen.
"There are so many conflicting things going on with Japan," said Hazelton, referring to the trade situation.

Dollar/mark took off early in the day on a surprisingly employment report as American companies added 316,000 jobs to their payrolls in July, pushing the unemployment rate 0.2-percent lower to 4.8 percent. This matched the level recorded in May, the lowest in nearly a quarter century.
In late trading, the dollar was quoted at 1.8620/30 marks versus 1.8330/34 at the open, and at 118.35/45 yen vs. 119.00/05.

Traders said the strong U.S. expansion and concern about Europe's sluggish economy and uncertainty about the planned single currency should continue to fuel dollar buying, at least versus the European currencies.
Dollar/Paris also surged to its highest level since November 1989, with an intraday high of 6.29.
Dollar/Swiss rocketed to 1.5295, setting a four-year high and topping the 1.5261 level made earlier this week.

The other winner of the day was sterling which gained more than two pfennigs to end at 3.04 marks as outgoing Bank of England deputy governor Howard Davies said the British economy may need somewhat higher interest rates.
The dollar closed at 1.5262/72 Swiss francs vs. 1.5224/29 at the open. It ended at Canadian $1.3809/14 vs. C$1.3773/78.
Cable ended at $1.6310/20 vs. $1.6345/55 while the Australian dollar finished at $0.7392/97 vs. $0.7420/25.
